
=================================================================
#55 Alji  (65)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: founder fairy tale
Logline: Roosters don’t crow at night. In the woods west of the city, one does.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Bidam said there was no Kim. He was right for about a hundred and twenty years. Then, one spring night, King Talhae wakes to a rooster crowing in the woods west of the city.
[1] Seok Talhae: Hogong. There’s a rooster in Sirim. / Go and see what it wants.
[2] Hogong: Majesty, it’s a rooster. It wants— / …Yes, Majesty. Going.
[3] ¶ At first light Hogong walks into Sirim with a lantern he no longer needs, and finds a small box of gold hanging from a branch, and a white rooster underneath it, crowing at nothing.
[4] ¶ They bring the box to the king and open it, and inside is a little boy, handsome and wide awake, who looks at the king as if the king were the one who had turned up in a box.
[5] Seok Talhae: Well. / I came in a box too, you know. Mine was bigger.
[6] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum): Hogong came back and reported it. The king had the chest brought and opened, and inside was a little boy of remarkable looks. The king was glad and said to those around him: “Is this not Heaven sending me a fine heir?” And he took him in and raised him.❞
[7] ¶ Because he came out of a golden box, he is given the surname **Kim**, gold. Because he is a child, he is called **Alji**. The wood where the rooster crowed is renamed Gyerim, Rooster Wood, and for a while the whole country goes by that name.
[8] ¶ The boy grows up in the palace, quick and easy to like. The court notices. Talhae has sons of his own. He also has ministers who can count.
[9] Seok Talhae: Alji. The ministers say Heaven sent you to me as an heir. / Heaven sends a great many things. It sent me a magpie. / So. Do you want the chair?
[10] Kim Alji: …No, Majesty. / Your sons were here first.
[11] Seok Talhae: Ha! First. I came in a chest. You came in a box. / Nobody in this palace was here first except six old men, and they don’t want the chair either.
[12] Kim Alji: Then I’ll wait.
[13] Seok Talhae: How long?
[14] Kim Alji: As long as it takes. Gold doesn’t rust, Majesty.
[15] ¶ So Alji does not get the throne, and by every account he never asks again. It takes his line seven generations to reach the crown. When they do, they keep it for six hundred years, call themselves the Kims of Surabol, and look down on a family from Gaya who have the same name for a different reason. Many generations after that, one of them is a man named Chunchu.
[16] ¶ Under a certain hill beyond the city, the steam says the same word every time it leaves the water. Kim. It will be a long time before anybody answers it.
[17] ── SCENE: Gyerim ──
[18] ¶ In the coronation year the wood is still there, beside the Moon Palace. After dark the new king walks his son through it.
[19] King Muyeol: Park came out of an egg. Seok came out of a chest and stole a house. We came out of a box and waited seven generations for a chair. / Every house that ever wore this crown arrived in something. That’s why they count bones here, Bupmin. / The people who were here first need something to count.
[20] King Munmu: And you, Father? You didn’t come out of anything.
[21] King Muyeol: No. Tired men in Tang silk voted me in. / So I’ll have to earn it the vulgar way. Three kingdoms, one crown. / Starting with the one that keeps knocking.
[22] ¶ **Across the border in Sabi, a funeral bell. For three years the king can’t sign a thing. The clans already have a list…!**
